title: Shafakat Husain v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J. and Dinesh Pathak, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to clause 6.14; coercive action stayed.
headnote: A writ challenging a DVVNL demand notice was disposed of without examining the merits. The consumer, who offered to pay in instalments, was given liberty to apply to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks; that officer is to consider the representation in accordance with law within four weeks, and no coercive action is to be taken on the demand in the meantime.
facts: The petitioner challenged a demand notice dated 25 November 2020 issued against him by the Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Firozabad, and sought a mandamus restraining harassment in connection with that demand. He submitted that he was ready to deposit the outstanding amount in instalments. Counsel for the power corporation submitted that Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides for payment of dues in instalments, and that the petitioner should approach the Executive Engineer.

holding_units.holding: Without entering the merits of the demand, a consumer willing to pay electricity dues in instalments may be relegated to Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The designated officer must consider a representation made within two weeks and pass an appropriate order in accordance with law within four weeks; meanwhile no coercive action is to be taken on the impugned demand.

principle_tags.application: The petitioner, ready to deposit the demanded amount in instalments, was directed to apply under Clause 6.14; the Executive Engineer is to consider that representation in accordance with law, with coercive recovery stayed in the meantime.

not_decided.point: Validity of the demand notice dated 25.11.2020
not_decided.note: The Court expressly disposed of the writ without entering into the merits.
